skill.name: interview-me
skill.description: Extracts what the user actually wants instead of what they think they should want. Achieves this through one-question-at-a-time interview until ~95% confidence about the underlying intent. Use when an ask is underspecified ("build me X" without "for whom" or "why now"), when the user explicitly invokes ("interview me", "grill me", "are we sure?", "stress-test my thinking"), or when you catch yourself silently filling in ambiguous requirements before any plan, spec, or code exists.

content.user_title: Clarify User Intent Before You Build
content.value_statement: Underspecified requests cause teams to build the wrong outcome and discover misalignment late. This skill runs a focused, one-question interview that turns ambiguity into confirmed intent.
actual_capabilities: Identifies missing context about the user, motivation, success criteria, and constraints.
States a working hypothesis with a confidence estimate before asking questions.
Asks one focused question at a time and explains the reasoning behind each guess.
Detects vague, conventional, or best-practice answers that may hide the real goal.
Restates outcome, user, timing, success, constraints, and scope exclusions for confirmation.
Routes confirmed intent toward downstream planning or specification work.
limitations: Requires a live, responsive user for the interview process.
Does not produce a technical specification, implementation plan, or task list.
Cannot resolve missing information when the user cannot provide meaningful answers.
Does not replace domain expertise or stakeholder approval.

use_cases.title: Shape a Product Request
use_cases.description: Turn a broad product idea into a confirmed outcome, target user, success measure, and explicit scope boundary.

use_cases.title: Clarify an Engineering Task
use_cases.description: Expose hidden assumptions before planning or coding, especially when a familiar request could represent several different solutions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Stakeholder Handoff
use_cases.description: Capture confirmed intent in the requester’s language so another collaborator can continue with fewer misunderstandings.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Intent Interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about this request one question at a time. State your hypothesis and confidence before the first question.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify a broad request before discussing solutions.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge My Assumptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use interview-me to find assumptions in my request. Probe who benefits, why now, success criteria, constraints, and what is out of scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an ambiguous feature request for planning.

prompt_templates.title: Test the Real Goal
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about this proposed solution. Treat the solution as a hypothesis and identify the underlying problem before accepting the requested artifact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: determine whether the requested solution matches the actual need.

prompt_templates.title: Confirm and Handoff Intent
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a one-question interview until you can predict my next three answers. Restate the confirmed intent with outcome, user, why now, success, constraint, and out of scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: create a handoff-ready intent statement after explicit confirmation.

output_examples.input: Build me a dashboard for our metrics.
output_examples.output: Hypothesis: You need a way to track experiment status and early signals. Confidence: about 30 percent because the audience, metrics, and success measure are unclear. Question: Who will use this dashboard?
Question: If you did not need to justify the decision, what result would you actually want? Guess: You may value faster completion more than broad future flexibility.

output_examples.input: I want a handoff document after the interview.
output: Outcome: Track active experiments and their early signals.
User: The requester uses it during weekly reviews.
Why now: Information is spread across several documents.
Success: The requester can find every active experiment in one place.
Out of scope: Automated reporting and implementation planning.

best_practices: Start with a defensible hypothesis and state what remains unknown.
Ask one focused question at a time, with a reasoned guess attached.
Require explicit confirmation of the concrete restatement before handing off.
anti_patterns: Do not batch several discovery questions into one message.
Do not accept vague agreement or delegation as explicit confirmation.
Do not create a plan or specification before intent is confirmed.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a request is underspecified, conventional, or likely to hide competing priorities.

faq.question: How many questions will it ask?
faq.answer: It asks only as many focused questions as needed to reach shared understanding.

faq.question: Can it interview users in batch mode?
faq.answer: No. It requires a live, responsive interaction and asks one question at a time.

faq.question: What does the final output contain?
faq.answer: The final output is a confirmed intent statement covering outcome, user, timing, success, constraints, and scope exclusions.

faq.question: Does it write a project plan?
faq.answer: No. It clarifies intent first, then supports a handoff to planning or specification skills.

faq.question: What happens when I say whatever you think?
faq.answer: The skill treats that response as delegation and asks concrete alternatives instead of treating it as a decision.
